title: S285 Appendix D. Use of SDP for RTSP Session Descriptions
parent_path: S285 Appendix D. Use of SDP for RTSP Session Descriptions

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The session-level URI MUST be different from any media-level URI.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The presence of a session-level control attribute MUST be interpreted as support for aggregated control.
actions: interpret session-level control attribute as support for aggregate control

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The control attribute MUST be present on the media level unless the presentation only contains a single media stream; in which case, the attribute MAY be present on the session level only and then also apply to that single media stream.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The control attribute MUST be present on the media level unless the presentation only contains a single media stream; in which case, the attribute MAY be present on the session level only and then also apply to that single media stream.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This attribute MAY contain either relative or absolute URIs, following the rules and conventions set out in RFC 3986 [RFC3986].

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations MUST look for a base URI in the following order: 1. the RTSP Content-Base field; 2. the RTSP Content-Location field; 3. the RTSP Request-URI.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If this attribute contains only an asterisk (*), then the URI MUST be treated as if it were an empty embedded URI; thus, it will inherit the entire base URI.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the session is over multicast, the port number indicated SHOULD be used for reception.
actions: use port number from SDP m= line for reception

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY try to override the destination port, through the Transport header.
actions: include overriding destination port in Transport header of SETUP request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The servers MAY allow this: the response will indicate whether or not this is allowed.
actions: indicate in SETUP response whether destination port override is allowed or denied

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the session is unicast, the port numbers are the ones RECOMMENDED by the server to the client, about which receiver ports to use; the client MUST still include its receiver ports in its SETUP request.
actions: recommend receiver port numbers to client in SDP m= line

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the session is unicast, the port numbers are the ones RECOMMENDED by the server to the client, about which receiver ports to use; the client MUST still include its receiver ports in its SETUP request.
actions: include client receiver ports in SETUP request Transport header

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY ignore this recommendation.
actions: optionally ignore server-recommended receiver ports and use client-chosen ports in SETUP request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server has no preference, it SHOULD set the port number value to zero.

statements.subject: rtsp
statements.description: The currently defined combinations are discussed in Appendix C; further combinations MAY be specified.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Thus, all RTSP SDP SHOULD have an "a=recvonly" attribute when using the PLAY mode defined in this document.
actions: include a=recvonly attribute in RTSP SDP

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For presentations that contain media streams of the same duration, the range attribute SHOULD only be used at the session level.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In case of different lengths, the range attribute MUST be given at media level for all media and SHOULD NOT be given at the session level.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In case of different lengths, the range attribute MUST be given at media level for all media and SHOULD NOT be given at the session level.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the attribute is present at both media level and session level, the media-level values MUST be used.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST take care to provide RTSP Range (see Section 18.40) values that are consistent with what is presented in the SDP for the content.
actions: provide RTSP Range header values consistent with SDP a=range attribute for content

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY override that property in the response to a PLAY request using the correct values in the Range header.
actions: include correct Range header values in PLAY response to override non-seekable property

statements.subject: rtsp
statements.description: The units and their values are as defined in Section 4.4.1, Section 4.4.2, and Section 4.4.3 and MAY be extended with further formats.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Any open-ended range (start-), i.e., without stop range, is of unspecified duration and MUST be considered as content that is not seekable unless this property is overridden.
actions: treat content with open-ended range as not seekable

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Multiple instances carrying different clock formats MAY be included at either session or media level.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For on-demand content, the server SHOULD indicate a stop time value for which it guarantees the description to be valid and a start time that is equal to or before the time at which the DESCRIBE request was received.
actions: set SDP stop time to a value guaranteeing description validity
set SDP start time to value <= DESCRIBE request receipt time

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY also indicate start and stop times of 0, meaning that the session is always available.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For sessions that are of live type, i.e., specific start time, unknown stop time, likely not seekable, the "t=" and "r=" field SHOULD be used to indicate the start time of the event.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The stop time SHOULD be given so that the live event will have ended at that time, while still not being unnecessary far into the future.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a multicast address is specified, the client SHOULD use this address in any SETUP request as destination address, including any additional parameters, such as TTL.
actions: use SDP multicast address as destination in SETUP Transport header
include TTL and additional parameters from SDP in SETUP Transport header

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For on-demand unicast streams and some multicast streams, the destination address MAY be specified by the client via the SETUP request, thus overriding any specified address.
actions: optionally specify destination address in SETUP Transport header to override SDP c= address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To identify streams without a fixed destination address, where the client is required to specify a destination address, the "c=" field SHOULD be set to a null value.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For addresses of type "IP4", this value MUST be "0.0.0.0"; and for type "IP6", this value MUST be "0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0" (can also be written as "::"), i.e., the unspecified address according to RFC 4291 [RFC4291].

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For addresses of type "IP4", this value MUST be "0.0.0.0"; and for type "IP6", this value MUST be "0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0" (can also be written as "::"), i.e., the unspecified address according to RFC 4291 [RFC4291].

statements.subject: session
statements.description: It is RECOMMENDED that grouped media are handled by aggregate control, to give the client the ability to control either the whole presentation or single media.
actions: use aggregate control to handle grouped media
